channel.title: Microbial Metallomics — Reviews
channel.description: New writing, research summaries, and paper reviews from Microbial Metallomics.

item.title: Iron Fortification and the Kenyan Infant Gut Microbiome
item.description: A full review of Jaeggi et al. (Gut 2015): iron-fortified porridge increased pathogenic E. coli and enterobacteria, cut bifidobacteria, and inflamed the gut in Kenyan infants.

item.title: Prenatal Tobacco Exposure and the Child Gut Microbiome
item.description: Prenatal smoking and childhood gut taxa were associated in an observational cohort; the responsible exposure components remain unresolved.

item.title: Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Intestinal Inflammation
item.description: A 2024 PROGRESS cohort study links prenatal copper and cesium exposure, interacting with specific gut microbes, to elevated fecal calprotectin in children.

item.title: Prenatal Acetaminophen, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Cognition
item.description: GESTE cohort links prenatal acetaminophen and caffeine to childhood gut microbiome shifts and cognition; Proteobacteria abundance modified WISC-IV scores.

item.title: Pediatric Gut Microbiome Composition in Health: What a Systematic Review Reveals
item.description: A systematic review of 42 studies finds geography, diet, and 16S sequencing method, not age, shape healthy children's Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes gut profiles.

item.title: Lactoferrin vs. Ferrous Sulfate Through a Metallomics Lens
item.description: Meta-analyses show oral lactoferrin can match or outperform ferrous sulfate for iron repletion, lowering IL-6 and hepcidin with fewer gut side effects.

item.title: Lactobacillus plantarum 299v and Oral Iron Therapy Tolerance
item.description: A randomized trial shows the probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum 299v reduces oral iron side effects and improves iron status in iron-deficiency anemia patients.

item.title: Iron- and Zinc-Biofortified Foods and the Gut Microbiota
item.description: Systematic review of iron/zinc-biofortified bean and wheat diets in the Gallus gallus model: staples raised SCFA-producing Lactobacillus and cut enteric pathogens.

item.title: Iron Supplements and the Gut Microbiome in Reproductive-Age Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: A 21-day randomized placebo-controlled trial found ferrous fumarate did not significantly alter fecal microbiome composition in Australian reproductive-age women.

item.title: Iron Fortification, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Diarrhea Risk
item.description: Iron fortification shifts the infant gut microbiome toward enterobacteria and pathogenic E. coli, cutting protective bifidobacteria and raising diarrhea risk.

item.title: Intestinal Biomarkers and the Non-Motor Phenotype of Parkinson's Disease
item.description: Parkinson's patients with constipation show higher fecal calprotectin, reduced SCFAs, lower gut diversity, and greater IBD genetic risk, linking gut inflammation to non-motor severity.

item.title: HERFD-XAS: High-Resolution X-ray Speciation of Biological Metals
item.description: HERFD-XAS sharpens X-ray absorption spectra by rejecting core-hole broadening, resolving mercury, selenium, and arsenic speciation in dilute biological samples for metallomics.

item.title: Gut Microbiome and Childhood Stunting in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
item.description: Systematic review of 14 studies links childhood stunting in LMICs to inflammatory gut pathobionts and depleted butyrate producers, driving impaired linear growth.

item.title: Childhood Blood Metals and the Gut Microbiome: Evidence from the GESTE Cohort
item.description: GESTE cohort links childhood blood metals (Mn, Se, Cd, Hg, Pb) to gut microbiome composition in 6-7 year olds; manganese and selenium tied to bacterial phyla.

item.title: A Multi-Omics + MR Enterography Model for Predicting Bowel Damage in Crohn's Disease
item.description: Two-center study fusing gut microbiome, fecal and serum metabolomics, and MR enterography into a model predicting cumulative Crohn's bowel damage (AUC 0.857).

item.title: The Human Microbiome Across Body Sites: Gut, Skin, Oral, Vaginal and Lung
item.description: How the human microbiome differs across the gut, skin, oral, vaginal and lung niches, how it is acquired and disrupted, and why heavy-metal exposure matters.

item.title: Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Depression
item.description: A Mexico City birth-cohort study links a prenatal zinc-cobalt profile plus specific gut bacteria to 15.4% higher childhood depression scores at ages 9-11.

item.title: Prenatal Lead Exposure and the Childhood Gut Microbiome
item.description: Prenatal lead exposure is negatively linked to the childhood gut microbiome: metagenomics from a Mexico City cohort ties maternal Pb to fewer beneficial bacteria.

item.title: Prebiotics Blunt the Gut Cost of Iron-Fortified Cereal in Kenyan Infants
item.description: In a Kenyan infant RCT, adding prebiotic GOS/FOS to iron-fortified cereal raised iron absorption 60% and reduced gut inflammation, pathogens, and dysbiosis.

item.title: Nutritional Immunity and Trace Metals in Infection
item.description: How the host uses iron, zinc, manganese and copper handling as nutritional immunity to starve or poison pathogens, plus metal-based therapeutic strategies.

item.title: Metal Availability and Immune Function During Infection
item.description: How zinc, iron, manganese, and copper availability shapes neutrophil and macrophage function during infection through nutritional immunity, calprotectin, and phagosomal metal handling.

item.title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Transfusion-Dependent Thalassemia
item.description: Clinical review of deferoxamine, deferiprone, and deferasirox for transfusion iron overload in thalassemia, covering cardiac and hepatic iron outcomes measured by MRI T2*.

item.title: Heavy Metals and the Gut Microbiota: A Systematic Review
item.description: Systematic review of 12 human studies links arsenic, lead, mercury, and cadmium exposure to gut microbiota dysbiosis, leaky gut, and disease, with dietary mitigation.

item.title: Gallium as an Iron Mimic: Disrupting Pseudomonas Iron Metabolism in Cystic Fibrosis
item.description: Gallium substitutes for iron to sabotage Pseudomonas aeruginosa iron metabolism. A Phase 1 CF trial (Goss et al., Sci Transl Med 2018) found IV gallium improved lung function.

item.title: Copper in Infectious Disease: Both Sides of the Penny
item.description: How the immune system weaponizes copper against pathogens: macrophage copper bursts, phagosomal intoxication, fungal copper detox, and copper nutritional immunity.

item.title: Arsenic Exposure Reshapes the Gut Microbiome of Bangladeshi Children, Enriching Resistance-Carrying E. coli
item.description: Arsenic-exposed Bangladeshi children carry more gut Proteobacteria and E. coli bearing arsenic-resistance (ars) and antibiotic-resistance-like genes, a metal-microbiome case study.

item.title: Spatial Metallomics in Colorectal Cancer: Copper-Immune and Iron-EMT Pathways
item.description: Spatial metallomics pairs LA-ICP-TOF-MS with Visium transcriptomics in colorectal cancer, mapping copper to immune genes and iron to EMT at the tumor front.

item.title: Proteome-Scale Mapping of Iron-Binding Proteins in Bread Wheat
item.description: A proteome-wide scan of bread wheat mapped ~600 iron-binding proteins with Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites coordinated by His, Glu, Asp and Cys, aiding metallomics.

item.title: [NiFe]-Hydrogenase Cofactor Biosynthesis and the Hyp Maturation Proteins (HypA-F) in E. coli
item.description: How E. coli builds the NiFe(CN)2CO cofactor of [NiFe]-hydrogenases: the HypA-F maturation proteins, cyanide and CO ligand synthesis, and nickel insertion.

item.title: The Zinc Clasp: How Zn2+ Shapes T-Cell Signaling
item.description: The zinc clasp is a Zn2+-bridged interface that tethers the kinase Lck to CD4 and CD8 coreceptors, a labile-zinc switch central to T-cell activation and immunity.

item.title: The Iron Metalloproteome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Under Oxic and Anoxic Conditions
item.description: Native metalloproteomics maps how Pseudomonas aeruginosa partitions iron across four protein complexes, with denitrification raising iron demand in anoxia.

item.title: Nitric Oxide Sensing by the [4Fe-4S] Regulator ArnR
item.description: ArnR uses a [4Fe-4S] cluster to sense nitric oxide: NO nitrosylates the cluster, abolishing DNA binding and derepressing nitrate-respiration and hmp genes.

item.title: Maternal Metallomic Profiles in Pregnancy with Obesity: A Secondary Analysis of UPBEAT
item.description: UPBEAT analysis profiled 18 serum metals in 755 pregnant women with obesity: elevated manganese linked to antepartum hemorrhage, phosphorus to NICU care.

item.title: Iron-Sulfur Clusters and Oxygen in Human Disease
item.description: How iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster biogenesis and oxygen shape human disease: NFS1 in lung cancer, hyperoxia injury, and hypoxia therapy for Friedreich ataxia.
